cases.section: supermemo 20 rules - ill-formulated Dead Sea example
cases.sourceText: Salt lake located on the border between Israel and Jordan. Its shoreline is the lowest point on the Earth's surface, averaging 396 m below sea level. It is 74 km long. It is seven times as salty (30% by volume) as the ocean. Its density keeps swimmers afloat. Only simple organisms can live in its saline waters.
cases.frontPrefix: Why can the Dead Sea keep

carding.rationale: A dense multi-fact blob. The prefix gestures at the 'keeps swimmers afloat' fact, not the first (location) fact. The copilot must ground on the targeted sentence and produce an atomic, non-leaking card.
plausibleUserPrefixes: Why can the Dead Sea keep

preferredCards.front: Why can the Dead Sea keep swimmers afloat?

badButPlausibleCards.front: Why can the Dead Sea be described as a salt lake located on the border between?
badButPlausibleCards.whyBad: Grabbed the first fact in the blob, not the gestured fact; the Front also leaks the answer.

badButPlausibleCards.front: Why can the Dead Sea keep swimmers afloat?
badButPlausibleCards.whyBad: Back restates the Front instead of giving an atomic answer.

cases.sourceText: The forgetting curve, first described by Hermann Ebbinghaus, hypothesizes the decline of memory retention over time. Memory of new material drops steeply within the first day and then levels off.

carding.rationale: Dense/definitional material the maintainer prefers as a cloze deletion rather than a single Q&A.

preferredCards.text: The forgetting curve, first described by {{c1::Hermann Ebbinghaus}}, hypothesizes the {{c2::decline}} of memory retention over {{c3::time}}.

cases.sourceText: The spacing effect is the finding that information is remembered better when study is spread out over time than when the same amount is crammed into a single session.

carding.rationale: A definitional sentence that makes a clean cloze deletion.

preferredCards.text: The {{c1::spacing effect}} is the finding that information is remembered better when study is {{c2::spread out over time}} than when crammed into a single session.
